title: Ariadne: A Hotness-Aware and Size-Adaptive Compressed Swap Technique for Fast Application Relaunch and Reduced CPU Usage on Mobile Devices
problem: Mobile devices under memory pressure use ZRAM (RAM-based compressed swap) to defer app eviction, but ZRAM prolongs relaunch latency and wastes CPU time because it applies uniform compression settings regardless of data hotness, does not differentiate compression chunk size, and lacks prefetching of soon-to-be-needed decompressed data.
motivation: Application relaunch latency and CPU usage for compression/decompression directly impact mobile user experience, and growing app memory footprints exacerbate memory pressure on fixed mobile DRAM budgets.
method: Ariadne tracks which memory pages get used frequently when an app relaunches (labeled 'hot'), sometimes ('warm'), or rarely ('cold'), and remembers these labels for future relaunches. It compresses hot and warm memory using small chunks that decompress quickly on the critical launch path, while using large chunks for cold data to save more storage space. It also predicts which pages will be needed next during startup and decompresses them in advance, so this decompression happens in parallel with the app launching.
key_novelty: The core idea is to compress relaunch-critical data into small fast-decompressing chunks while compressing rarely-used data into larger high-compression chunks, and to predict which data is needed next so decompression can happen in the background.
contributions: Observation that anonymous data has stable hotness between consecutive relaunches and exhibits spatial locality during relaunch
Low-overhead hotness classification scheme for ZRAM pages without significant runtime profiling cost
Size-adaptive compression assigning different chunk sizes per hotness tier to balance decompression speed and compression ratio
Proactive decompression predictor reducing relaunch latency by 50% and CPU usage of compression/decompression by 15% over ZRAM on Google Pixel 7 (Android 14)

metrics.speedup: 50% reduction in application relaunch latency vs ZRAM
metrics.other: 15% reduction in CPU usage for compression/decompression vs ZRAM

limitations: Evaluated on a single device (Google Pixel 7); generalization to different SoC memory configurations and Android versions is not discussed.
primary_theme: hotness-aware adaptive compressed swap for mobile application relaunch optimization
